newsitem.title: UK: Five hurt in Guinness helicopter crash landing.
newsitem.headline: Five hurt in Guinness helicopter crash landing.

text.p: Five people were injured when a helicopter taking part in a promotional trip for brewing firm Guinness Ireland crash-landed near Enniskillen in Northern Ireland on Monday, police said.

A company spokesman said in Dublin the managing director of Guinness Northern Ireland, Brian Duffy, was one of the passengers but did not appear to have been seriously hurt. He was able to walk away from the crash.
"Two people are ill but stable. One is stable. The other two people have minor injuries," a spokeswoman at Enniskillen's Erne Hospital told Reuters.
The helicopter was believed to be carrying five people -- the pilot, the Guinness executive and three journalists.

The hospital spokeswoman said that those classifed "ill but stable" would be transferred to a Belfast hospital for further assessment but their condition had not worsened. None of the injuries was life-threatening.
The helicopter was one of three aircraft taking part in the launch of a marketing campaign for Guinness, a company spokesman said.
"It would appear that a bird flew into the rear rotor of the helicopter, and the helicopter came down."

The injured journalists were Barbara McCann, GMTV reporter in Belfast, Jim McDowell, Northern Ireland editor of the Dublin-published Sunday World, and Joe Kearney of the Belfast morning paper, the Irish News.

Liam Creagh, GMTV Ireland correspondent, who visited the hospital later, said McCann was "ill with a back injury" and had remained conscious throughout the ordeal. "She is now being transferred to Belfast for tests."
He said McDowell's wife, Lindy, who is also a journalist, was in one of the other helicopters. She witnessed the accident and saw her husband lying injured when her aircraft landed.
She told Creagh that he sustained a back injury which was not thought to be serious.
